name: Insider Threat and Risk Architecture
description: What a comprehensive insider program does, and what each European jurisdiction requires of it. Pillars, measures, and the controls a jurisdiction makes of them.

states.established: A source that has been read sets the condition.
states.not covered: The record was searched here and says nothing.
states.unread: A source has been identified and is not yet worked in.
states.open: This pairing has not been examined.

pillars.name: Governance and mandate
pillars.summary: The authority under which an insider program operates, its ownership, and the record of both.

measures.name: Program charter and mandate
measures.what: The instrument that establishes the program, states its authority, names its sponsor, and bounds what it may reach.

cells.requirement: The Union-funded manual addresses how a program is structured, and states no legal basis for any of it.

sources.title: Insider Threat Program Development Manual
sources.establishes: The structure of an insider program, as the closest thing to doctrine issued under European Union funding, unrevised since 2019.

cells.requirement: The charter is written to be reviewed against rather than filed: governance and culture are set out as things a program is measured on, not as preamble to the controls.

sources.title: Insider Risk Mitigation Framework
sources.establishes: A structure for an insider program that an organization reviews itself against, with governance and culture as foundations rather than adjuncts.

measures.name: Declared perimeter
measures.what: The single account of what the program does, what it does not do, and on what authority, written to be shown outside it.

measures.name: Cross-functional governance body
measures.what: The standing body in which the functions a program touches meet and decide together: security, human resources, legal, compliance, and technology. What makes it this measure rather than a mailing list is that it decides, and that it decides in one room rather than one function at a time.

cells.requirement: The group is named and its membership drawn: physical and information security, technology, human resources, vetting, facilities, contracts, procurement, finance, counter fraud, legal, training, communications, and a staff or trade union representative. What the group decides is not stated.

sources.title: Insider Risk Practitioners and Stakeholders
sources.establishes: That a program needs a senior stakeholder group drawn from named functions, and a director who carries the board's strategy into policy.

measures.name: Roles and decision rights
measures.what: The statement of which decisions the program may take, of the role entitled to take each, and of the person holding that role. The decisions are the ones the framework names elsewhere: to open a case on a person, to reach for the content of what they wrote, to withdraw their access before any finding, and to recommend a consequence.

cells.requirement: One board member holds overall responsibility for protective security, and a non-executive director acts as an independent champion for it. Below them a director carries the strategy into policy, and senior staff in each business area answer for the risk assessment and for implementation in their own.

sources.title: Insider Risk Practitioners and Stakeholders
sources.establishes: That a program needs a senior stakeholder group drawn from named functions, and a director who carries the board's strategy into policy.

sources.title: Board Engagement and Governance
sources.establishes: That one board member holds overall responsibility for protective security and is regularly engaged with the program, with a non-executive director as an independent champion.

cells.requirement: The technician who reached into the accounts held the role and not the instruction. A signed confidentiality undertaking is not the documented instruction the Regulation asks of anyone processing on the controller’s behalf.

sources.title: Provvedimento del 17 aprile 2026, Framos Italia
sources.establishes: That a company mailbox left running after the employment ends is a processing needing a ground of its own, and that a smooth handover and the chance of wanting something later are not one.

measures.name: Shared definitions and severity scale
measures.what: A written agreement among the functions on what constitutes an event, what constitutes a condition, and what a given severity denotes.

cells.requirement: Five principles are offered as a shared basis, with intentional and unintentional events placed on one spectrum of intent.

sources.title: NPSA Changes to Insider Risk Definitions
sources.establishes: Revised definitions of insider, insider risk, insider threat, and insider event, organized around intent.

cells.requirement: The definitions are agreed to be used consistently, and intentional and unintentional events are held on one spectrum so that a severity scale does not have to choose between them.

sources.title: Setting the Foundations: Five Principles for a Shared Approach to Insider Risk
sources.establishes: Five principles offered as a shared basis, with intentional and unintentional events placed on one spectrum of intent.

measures.name: Escalation triggers and owners
measures.what: The agreement, settled between the functions before any case exists, on which conditions pass out of the team that observed them, to whom they pass, and within what time. As distinct from moving a live matter upward during a response, which the incident pillar holds.

measures.name: Lawful basis register
measures.what: The record naming, for each stream of data the program collects and each use it puts that data to, the ground it rests on and the condition the jurisdiction attaches to that ground. Written before the collection starts, and held in a form that can be shown rather than asserted.

cells.requirement: A ground under article 6 has to be recorded for each stream the program collects, before it collects it, and the register has to survive the article 5(2) test of being shown rather than asserted.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, articles 5(2), 6, 12, 15, 35, and 88
sources.establishes: The grounds on which processing may rest, the burden of showing it, what a person asking has to be told and by when, when an impact assessment is owed, and the leave each member state has to set its own employment rule.

sources.title: Opinion 2/2017 on data processing at work (WP249)
sources.establishes: That consent is rarely a valid ground in employment, and how legitimate interests are weighed against privacy across nine scenarios of workplace monitoring.

cells.requirement: The national employment provision cannot carry the register on its own: the ground recorded has to be one that stands under article 6 itself, the employer’s legitimate interests among them.

sources.title: Urteil 8 AZR 209/21
sources.establishes: That legitimate interests can carry a test on live employee data, and that the national employment provision fails the article 88 conditions.

cells.requirement: Only data directly necessary for the employment relationship may be processed, and no exception to that test can be made even with the employee’s consent.

sources.title: Laki yksityisyyden suojasta työelämässä (759/2004)
sources.establishes: One act for the whole subject, holding processing to what is directly necessary, naming the conditions for cameras and for opening the employer's electronic mail, and putting technical monitoring through a cooperation procedure before it is introduced.

cells.requirement: Four purposes are listed and the list is closed: unlawful or defamatory acts, the confidential economic interests of the undertaking, the security and technical functioning of its systems, and good faith observance of the rules it has set for using the technology.

sources.title: Convention collective de travail n° 81 du 26 avril 2002
sources.establishes: Four purposes for which network communication data may be monitored, collection in the aggregate rather than by name, and individualization as a separate operation with conditions of its own.

cells.requirement: A control measure rests on objective grounds in the circumstances of the undertaking and must not be a disproportionate burden on the person subject to it. No instruction and no agreement may depart from that to the worker’s detriment, so an agreement cannot be the ground for reaching further.

sources.title: Arbeidsmiljøloven, sections 9-1 and 9-2
sources.establishes: That a control measure needs objective grounds in the undertaking and must not be a disproportionate burden, and that it is discussed with the elected representatives, notified with its expected duration, and evaluated with them at intervals.

sources.title: Forskrift om arbeidsgivers innsyn i e-postkasse og annet elektronisk lagret materiale
sources.establishes: When an employer may look into a work mailbox or a worker's personal areas on its equipment, that monitoring of internet use is outside what it may do at all, and that the regulation cannot be contracted around.

measures.name: Impact assessment before deployment
measures.what: The written assessment, made before a measure operates and kept afterwards, of what it will do to the people subject to it: what it will collect about them, what may follow from what it collects, and what they can do about either. It is a document, and its absence is a finding on its own.

cells.requirement: The assessment has to be completed before the measure operates, not compiled after it, wherever the processing is likely to result in a high risk.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, articles 5(2), 6, 12, 15, 35, and 88
sources.establishes: The grounds on which processing may rest, the burden of showing it, what a person asking has to be told and by when, when an impact assessment is owed, and the leave each member state has to set its own employment rule.

cells.requirement: Its absence is enough on its own: a decision has turned on the missing procedural steps without reaching the purpose the processing served.

sources.title: Provvedimento n. 243
sources.establishes: That ninety days of metadata and browsing logs, kept without the procedural steps, draws a fine, the reasoning turning on the steps and not the purpose.

measures.name: Accountability evidence
measures.what: The material by which the program can show how it reached a decision about itself: a threshold set, an instrument chosen, a policy changed. As distinct from asserting that the decision was reached properly, and as distinct from the record of a single case, which the investigation pillar holds.

cells.requirement: The program has to be able to produce, for any decision, the material showing how it was reached. Holding a defensible view of it is not the same evidence.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, articles 5(2), 6, 12, 15, 35, and 88
sources.establishes: The grounds on which processing may rest, the burden of showing it, what a person asking has to be told and by when, when an impact assessment is owed, and the leave each member state has to set its own employment rule.

measures.name: Worker representative engagement
measures.what: The involvement of the body representing the workforce in the design of the program, as distinct from any instrument deployed under it.

cells.requirement: The body brought in is the social and economic committee, informed and consulted before the decision, and informed again before automated personnel management processing is introduced.

sources.title: Code du travail, articles L1121-1, L1222-4, and L2312-38
sources.establishes: Consultation of the social and economic committee before the decision, prior knowledge for the worker, and proportionality to the task.

cells.requirement: The body brought in is the works council, and its role is co-determination rather than consultation: the employer cannot proceed over its objection.

sources.title: Betriebsverfassungsgesetz, section 87(1)(6)
sources.establishes: Co-determination by the works council over the introduction and the use of technical devices intended to monitor conduct or performance.

cells.requirement: The body brought in is the union representation, and its agreement is the condition on which any instrument capable of remote monitoring may exist at all.

sources.title: Legge 20 maggio 1970, n. 300, article 4
sources.establishes: That an instrument from which remote monitoring may follow is permitted only for stated purposes, and only after a union agreement or an authorization.

cells.requirement: The body brought in is the works council, and its consent is required for the arrangement itself, not only for the instrument under it.

sources.title: Wet op de ondernemingsraden, article 27(1)(l)
sources.establishes: Consent of the works council for an arrangement directed at or merely suitable for observing presence, conduct, or performance.

cells.requirement: Camera surveillance, access control, other technical monitoring, and the use of electronic mail and the network go through the cooperation procedure before the employer decides. Where the cooperation acts do not apply, the employees or their representatives are heard first.

sources.title: Laki yksityisyyden suojasta työelämässä (759/2004)
sources.establishes: One act for the whole subject, holding processing to what is directly necessary, naming the conditions for cameras and for opening the employer's electronic mail, and putting technical monitoring through a cooperation procedure before it is introduced.

cells.requirement: The works council is informed on every aspect of the monitoring before the system is installed, and failing a works council the prevention committee, then the union delegation, then the workers.

sources.title: Convention collective de travail n° 81 du 26 avril 2002
sources.establishes: Four purposes for which network communication data may be monitored, collection in the aggregate rather than by name, and individualization as a separate operation with conditions of its own.

cells.requirement: The need for the measure, its design, its implementation, and any material change to it are discussed with the elected representatives as early as possible.

sources.title: Arbeidsmiljøloven, sections 9-1 and 9-2
sources.establishes: That a control measure needs objective grounds in the undertaking and must not be a disproportionate burden, and that it is discussed with the elected representatives, notified with its expected duration, and evaluated with them at intervals.

cells.requirement: The works council does not consent to a control measure as a step before it, but as the condition of its legal effect. What brings a measure inside the requirement is whether it touches human dignity.

sources.title: Arbeitsverfassungsgesetz, sections 96 and 96a
sources.establishes: That a control measure touching human dignity has no legal effect without the works council's consent, and that consent for automated processing and for assessment systems can be replaced by a conciliation board while consent under section 96 cannot.

measures.name: Notice before an algorithmic system is deployed
measures.what: Notice that a system of a named class is about to be put into use, owed to the representatives of the workforce and to the workers themselves. It falls due by reason of what the system is, so it is owed even where the representatives hold no right to be consulted, and even where they have already been consulted about the same system.

cells.requirement: Workers’ representatives have to be told before a high-risk system is put into use. The duty applies from 2 December 2027 for the Annex III categories.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, article 5(1)(f), Annex III(4), and article 26(7)
sources.establishes: That inferring emotions at work is prohibited, that employment and worker management are a high-risk category, and that representatives are told before deployment.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, amending the Artificial Intelligence Act
sources.establishes: When the high-risk obligations begin to apply, moved to December 2027, without altering what they classify.

measures.name: Program metrics and reporting
measures.what: What the program reports about its own operation to the body that governs it, and how often. Not what the program found, but how much of it there was, how long it took, and what it cost.

cells.requirement: The board member who holds the responsibility is to be regularly engaged with the people running the program and to hold a firm understanding of the risks it addresses. What is to be reported, and how often, is not stated.

sources.title: Board Engagement and Governance
sources.establishes: That one board member holds overall responsibility for protective security and is regularly engaged with the program, with a non-executive director as an independent champion.

measures.name: Periodic program review
measures.what: The revision of each component of the program at a stated interval.

cells.requirement: The framework is offered as something an organization reviews itself against, which makes the review a recurring act rather than a one-off inspection.

sources.title: Insider Risk Mitigation Framework
sources.establishes: A structure for an insider program that an organization reviews itself against, with governance and culture as foundations rather than adjuncts.

cells.requirement: The advice literature has itself been coded and characterised, so what guidance instructs can be examined rather than assumed.

sources.title: Systematic analysis of security advice on the topic of insider threats
sources.establishes: What the published guidance on insider threat actually instructs a reader to do, the advice literature being the object of study.

cells.requirement: The need for the measures is evaluated at intervals, and the evaluation is made together with the elected representatives rather than by the employer alone.

sources.title: Arbeidsmiljøloven, sections 9-1 and 9-2
sources.establishes: That a control measure needs objective grounds in the undertaking and must not be a disproportionate burden, and that it is discussed with the elected representatives, notified with its expected duration, and evaluated with them at intervals.

measures.name: Answering a request from the person
measures.what: The program's answer when a person asks what is held about them and what is done with it. It is a measure once there is a route the request reaches, someone answerable for the reply, a period inside which it is given, and a rule for what is withheld and on what ground. An answer given late, or given in part without saying what was taken out and why, is not an answer.

cells.requirement: The reply is owed within one month of the request. It can be extended by two more where the request is complex or the requests are many, but the extension and the reasons for it have to reach the person inside the first month. Where the program will not act at all, that is said inside the same month, with the routes to a complaint and to a court named.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, articles 5(2), 6, 12, 15, 35, and 88
sources.establishes: The grounds on which processing may rest, the burden of showing it, what a person asking has to be told and by when, when an impact assessment is owed, and the leave each member state has to set its own employment rule.

cells.requirement: Answering in stages across five months, and then handing over the correspondence purged of many elements without saying what had been taken out or why, was held not to be an answer.

sources.title: Provvedimento del 12 marzo 2026, ITAS Mutua
sources.establishes: That an answer given in stages and then handed over in part, without saying what was withheld, does not discharge the right of access, and that a five year backup of employee mail has to be disclosed to the people whose mail it holds.

pillars.name: Personnel security
pillars.summary: The measures directed at the person: what is verified before and during employment, what is asked of the people who manage them, what the program may hold about them, and what happens when they leave.

measures.name: Pre-employment screening
measures.what: The verification, before employment begins, of who the candidate is, that they may lawfully work, and that the account they give of their own history holds against evidence that does not come from them.

cells.requirement: Good practice treats screening at recruitment as the opening of a process rather than its completion.

sources.title: Ongoing Personnel Security: A Good Practice Guide
sources.establishes: Good practice for personnel security through employment rather than at the door, holding that protective monitoring should be proportionate.

cells.requirement: What needs the works council’s consent is the form put to the person: a personnel questionnaire asking beyond general particulars and the professional qualifications for the work intended. Verification carried out against a third party is not reached by it.

sources.title: Arbeitsverfassungsgesetz, sections 96 and 96a
sources.establishes: That a control measure touching human dignity has no legal effect without the works council's consent, and that consent for automated processing and for assessment systems can be replaced by a conciliation board while consent under section 96 cannot.

measures.name: Risk-tiered screening standards
measures.what: The written standard setting, for each level of exposure a role carries, what is checked and how far. Exposure, not seniority: a systems administrator two grades down reaches further than the director above them.

measures.name: Screening of privileged-role holders
measures.what: The further verification applied to a person because of what their access reaches, triggered by the entitlement itself rather than by the title attached to it.

measures.name: Screening during employment
measures.what: The repetition of verification, in whole or in part, at a stated interval and on stated events: a move into a role of greater exposure, a return after a long absence, and a concern raised through any of the routes the program keeps open.

cells.requirement: Contracting is covered alongside employment, so the standard is set for people the organization does not employ.

sources.title: Ongoing Personnel Security: A Good Practice Guide
sources.establishes: Good practice for personnel security through employment rather than at the door, holding that protective monitoring should be proportionate.

measures.name: Contractor and third-party personnel standards
measures.what: The personnel standard applied to people working in the organization under someone else's contract, carried through the contract that brings them in and evidenced by the party that employs them.

cells.requirement: Briefing at joining is treated as part of ongoing personnel security rather than as an administrative step.

sources.title: Ongoing Personnel Security: A Good Practice Guide
sources.establishes: Good practice for personnel security through employment rather than at the door, holding that protective monitoring should be proportionate.

measures.name: Onboarding security briefing
measures.what: What a person is told at the point of joining: what is observed about them and why, what is expected of them, what they are to report and to whom, and what follows from a breach. Recorded as having been given, since it is relied on afterwards.

measures.name: Role change and internal transfer
measures.what: The reassessment of what a person holds and owes when they move within the organization, including the withdrawal of what the previous role needed. Without the withdrawal, access accrues across a career and the person ends up reaching everywhere they have ever been.

cells.requirement: Access rights are modified on a change of employment and not only on its end, so a move inside the organization is an event the entitlements have to answer to.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Leaver process
measures.what: What happens when employment ends: access withdrawn, assets recovered, continuing obligations restated, and the accounts themselves closed within a period the organization has stated in advance.

cells.requirement: Exit is covered as a stage of personnel security, with what is withdrawn and what is restated set out together.

sources.title: Ongoing Personnel Security: A Good Practice Guide
sources.establishes: Good practice for personnel security through employment rather than at the door, holding that protective monitoring should be proportionate.

cells.requirement: The mailbox is closed when the employment ends, and stays open only where there is a particular need and only for a short period.

sources.title: Forskrift om arbeidsgivers innsyn i e-postkasse og annet elektronisk lagret materiale
sources.establishes: When an employer may look into a work mailbox or a worker's personal areas on its equipment, that monitoring of internet use is outside what it may do at all, and that the regulation cannot be contracted around.

cells.requirement: Leaving the account running after the employment ends is itself a processing and needs a ground of its own. Telling correspondents the person has gone, and keeping what may be wanted later, are not grounds, and running past the period the employer itself declared counts against it.

sources.title: Provvedimento del 17 aprile 2026, Framos Italia
sources.establishes: That a company mailbox left running after the employment ends is a processing needing a ground of its own, and that a smooth handover and the chance of wanting something later are not one.

cells.requirement: Access rights are modified on termination, and the register of what was granted is what the withdrawal is checked against.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Line management engagement
measures.what: The involvement of managers in noticing and raising concern about the people they supervise, structured by a named route, a stated threshold for using it, and instruction in both. Unstructured, it is a manager's instinct and reaches the program by chance.

cells.requirement: Line management is treated as the route by which concern reaches the program, which makes the manager part of the control.

sources.title: Ongoing Personnel Security: A Good Practice Guide
sources.establishes: Good practice for personnel security through employment rather than at the door, holding that protective monitoring should be proportionate.

measures.name: Line management records of personal circumstances
measures.what: Records of a worker's personal or family circumstances kept by the people who manage them, including those held outside any system the program runs: a manager's notebook, a shared drive, a private note.

cells.requirement: Notes kept by managers about a worker’s circumstances are processing like any other: outside a declared purpose and a lawful ground they have neither.

sources.title: Provvedimento n. 107, Amazon Italia Logistica
sources.establishes: That records of illness, union activity, and family circumstances kept by managers had no lawful basis, and attract the stricter regime.

measures.name: Records concerning trade union activity
measures.what: Records disclosing a worker's membership of a trade union or participation in its activity.

cells.requirement: A record touching union membership or activity falls in the stricter category, whatever the file it sits in and whoever wrote it.

sources.title: Provvedimento n. 107, Amazon Italia Logistica
sources.establishes: That records of illness, union activity, and family circumstances kept by managers had no lawful basis, and attract the stricter regime.

measures.name: Records concerning health held for security purposes
measures.what: Records of absence, illness, or fitness held for the purposes of the program.

cells.requirement: A record of absence or illness held for the program falls in the stricter category, and holding it for security purposes does not move it out.

sources.title: Provvedimento n. 107, Amazon Italia Logistica
sources.establishes: That records of illness, union activity, and family circumstances kept by managers had no lawful basis, and attract the stricter regime.

measures.name: Self-declaration of changed circumstances
measures.what: The route by which a worker reports a change in their own circumstances bearing on their position. It is a measure once it is named, reaches someone answerable for it, and states what becomes of what is declared.

cells.requirement: Reporting routes are covered as good practice, including the route by which a person reports about themselves.

sources.title: Ongoing Personnel Security: A Good Practice Guide
sources.establishes: Good practice for personnel security through employment rather than at the door, holding that protective monitoring should be proportionate.

cells.requirement: A standing route on which a worker reports about themselves becomes a personnel questionnaire once it asks beyond general particulars and qualifications, and introducing it then needs the works council’s consent.

sources.title: Arbeitsverfassungsgesetz, sections 96 and 96a
sources.establishes: That a control measure touching human dignity has no legal effect without the works council's consent, and that consent for automated processing and for assessment systems can be replaced by a conciliation board while consent under section 96 cannot.

pillars.name: Data and asset protection
pillars.summary: The protection of the information and assets the organization holds, and of the records the program itself generates.

measures.name: Identification of critical assets
measures.what: The list of the information, systems, and physical assets whose loss, alteration, or destruction would cause the organization material harm, and the record of who decided that and when. It is the list that is the measure. A program that knows in principle what matters, and cannot produce the list, does not hold it.

cells.requirement: Asset management is named among the measures an entity in scope has to take, alongside access control policies and human resources security in the same point. What the identification covers, and how far it goes, is left to the state of the art.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555, article 21
sources.establishes: That asset management, access control policies, human resources security, cryptography, and training are among the measures an entity in scope has to take, without saying what any of them holds.

measures.name: Information classification scheme
measures.what: The categories information is assigned to, the handling rules that follow from each, and what happens to information nobody has assigned. The default is part of the scheme: a category that only the careful apply leaves everything else outside it.

cells.requirement: A system of classification levels is laid down and every asset is placed in one, on confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity. The handling policy that follows runs from acquisition through use, storage, and transport to disposal, and reaches everyone who handles an asset.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Data discovery and inventory
measures.what: The location of regulated or sensitive data across the estate, as distinct from where policy assumes it is.

cells.requirement: The inventory is to be complete, accurate, up to date, and consistent, and changes to its entries are recorded so that they can be traced.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Access control and least privilege
measures.what: The entitlements each person actually holds, held to what their task requires and no wider. The measure is the state of the entitlements, not the policy that describes the state they ought to be in.

cells.requirement: Access control policies are named among the measures an entity in scope has to take, and for one class of entity the implementing rules say what they hold: rights assigned and revoked on need to know, least privilege, and separation of duties, modified on termination or change of employment, authorized by the relevant persons, limited in scope and duration for suppliers and visitors, held in a register, and logged.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555, article 21
sources.establishes: That asset management, access control policies, human resources security, cryptography, and training are among the measures an entity in scope has to take, without saying what any of them holds.

sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Privileged access management
measures.what: The separation, brokering, and time-bounding of access that exceeds ordinary entitlement.

cells.requirement: Privileged and system administration accounts carry policies of their own, strong identification and authentication among them, and the systems used to administer are kept for administration and separated from everything else.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Access recertification
measures.what: The periodic comparison of the access a person holds against the work they perform, and its adjustment.

cells.requirement: Access rights are reviewed at planned intervals and changed on organizational change, and the result of the review is documented together with the changes it called for.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
sources.establishes: What the directive's categories hold, in an annex setting out asset classification, the inventory, access control, privileged accounts, and removable media as requirements rather than as headings.

measures.name: Data loss prevention deployment
measures.what: The introduction of a capability that inspects content in motion, at rest, or in use, and acts on it against a policy.

cells.requirement: A ground under article 6 has to be identified before anything is collected through the loss prevention capability, and whatever more specific rule the member state has made under article 88 applies on top of it. Consent is not that ground in an employment relationship.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, articles 5(2), 6, 12, 15, 35, and 88

sources.establishes: That consent is rarely a valid ground in employment, and how legitimate interests are weighed against privacy across nine scenarios of workplace monitoring.

cells.requirement: Notice in advance, and a scope no wider than the purpose, are what a court will weigh if the use of the loss prevention capability is later examined.

sources.title: Bărbulescu v. Romania
sources.establishes: That private life and correspondence reach into the workplace, and the six criteria against which any monitoring measure is weighed.

cells.requirement: The social and economic committee has to be informed and consulted before the decision to deploy the capability, and the worker informed before content of theirs is inspected.

sources.title: Code du travail, articles L1121-1, L1222-4, and L2312-38
sources.establishes: Consultation of the social and economic committee before the decision, prior knowledge for the worker, and proportionality to the task.

cells.requirement: The works council has to agree before the loss prevention capability is introduced at all.

sources.title: Betriebsverfassungsgesetz, section 87(1)(6)

measures.name: Investigator competence
measures.what: The qualification, training, and independence of the people who conduct examinations.

pillars.name: Incident response
pillars.summary: The measures taken while an incident is open: containment, preservation, and notification.

measures.name: Insider incident playbooks
measures.what: The prepared sequences for the insider scenarios the program has decided it must be able to answer.

measures.name: Containment of an incident in progress
measures.what: The interruption of activity while it is happening, before its nature has been established.

measures.name: Withdrawal of access during a case
measures.what: The removal of a person's entitlements on suspicion, before any finding.

measures.name: Preservation of systems and records
measures.what: The holding of systems and records in the state they were in when the case opened.

measures.name: Coordination with security operations
measures.what: The joint working of the insider function with the teams that answer external intrusion.

measures.name: Notification to a supervisory authority
measures.what: The reporting of the incident, or of its handling, to an authority outside the organization.

measures.name: Notification to affected persons
measures.what: The telling of the people whose data or whose position the incident affected.

measures.name: Escalation to crisis management
measures.what: The passing of a matter to the body that decides for the organization as a whole.

measures.name: Post-incident review
measures.what: The examination, after the fact, of what the program saw, when, and what it did with it.

measures.name: Exercising the response
measures.what: The rehearsal of the playbooks against a scenario, with the people who would run them.

pillars.name: Consequence for the person
pillars.summary: The action taken against a person following a finding, and the basis on which it may be taken.

measures.name: Disciplinary action on monitoring evidence
measures.what: Action taken against a person on the basis of what the program observed, short of ending the relationship.

cells.requirement: A workplace disciplinary code has no legal effect without the works council’s consent, so what may follow from what the program observed is settled with the workforce before any case arises.

sources.title: Arbeitsverfassungsgesetz, sections 96 and 96a
sources.establishes: That a control measure touching human dignity has no legal effect without the works council's consent, and that consent for automated processing and for assessment systems can be replaced by a conciliation board while consent under section 96 cannot.

measures.name: Termination of employment
measures.what: The ending of the employment relationship on that basis.

cells.requirement: Dismissal on geolocation and dismissal after covert cameras have both been examined under article 8 and survived on their facts, which settles the method and not the outcome.

sources.title: Florindo de Almeida Vasconcelos Gramaxo v. Portugal
sources.establishes: That geolocation of a company vehicle, inside and outside working hours, did not violate article 8 on the facts, by four votes to three.

sources.title: López Ribalda and Others v. Spain
sources.establishes: That those criteria are weighed rather than counted, and that surveillance without notice can survive where a suspicion preceded it.

cells.requirement: Recordings may be used to substantiate the grounds for ending an employment relationship, and that use is stated as an exception to the purpose limitation and to the cooperation procedure.

sources.title: Laki yksityisyyden suojasta työelämässä (759/2004)
sources.establishes: One act for the whole subject, holding processing to what is directly necessary, naming the conditions for cameras and for opening the employer's electronic mail, and putting technical monitoring through a cooperation procedure before it is introduced.

measures.name: Consistency of outcomes
measures.what: The comparison of a proposed outcome against those reached in comparable cases.

measures.name: Reliance on material obtained in breach
measures.what: Reliance in proceedings on material gathered otherwise than as a legal requirement allowed.

cells.requirement: Material obtained in breach is not barred from proceedings by that alone, and a failure to inform the person does not bar it either.

sources.title: NTH Haustechnik GmbH v EM
sources.establishes: That a court may rely on data obtained in breach, subject to minimization of what it admits and to considering anonymization before disclosure.

cells.requirement: Material taken from personal correspondence could not be relied on, the Strasbourg case law being applied in the national setting.

sources.title: Sentenza n. 24204/2025
sources.establishes: That personal correspondence keeps its protection on company systems, and that what is taken from it cannot be relied on in proceedings.

measures.name: Referral to law enforcement
measures.what: The passing of a case, and the material supporting it, to an authority with powers the organization does not have.

measures.name: Civil recovery and injunctive action
measures.what: Proceedings brought by the organization to recover what was taken or to restrain its use.

measures.name: Communication of the outcome to the person
measures.what: The telling of the person what was concluded about them.

pillars.name: Awareness and training
pillars.summary: The instruction of the workforce concerning the program, and the record of it.

measures.name: Workforce awareness on insider risk
measures.what: The instruction of the workforce in what the program is, what it asks of them, and what it protects.

cells.requirement: A Union-funded platform carries an awareness module and downloadable templates, addressed mainly to transport, energy, and other critical infrastructure operators.

sources.title: Help2Protect
sources.establishes: Awareness and program-building material for critical infrastructure operators, with templates, and no legal basis stated for any of it.

cells.requirement: The Union-funded manual addresses the structure of a program rather than the conditions attached to one, and has not been revised since 2019.

sources.title: Insider Threat Program Development Manual
sources.establishes: The structure of an insider program, as the closest thing to doctrine issued under European Union funding, unrevised since 2019.

cells.requirement: Awareness is delivered as a course rather than a notice, in modules of ten to twenty minutes, with governance and leadership taught before the controls.

sources.title: Insider Risk Mitigation Digital Learning
sources.establishes: The mitigation framework taught in nine modules, with governance and leadership set as the foundation of personnel security.

cells.requirement: Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training are named among the measures an entity in scope has to take. What the directive asks to be taught is the security of systems, not insider risk.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555, article 21
sources.establishes: That asset management, access control policies, human resources security, cryptography, and training are among the measures an entity in scope has to take, without saying what any of them holds.

measures.name: Transparency notice on what is observed
measures.what: The account of the program's reach given to the persons subject to it.

cells.requirement: What the workforce is told after the procedure is the purpose of the monitoring, its introduction, the methods used, and the terms on which electronic mail and the network may be used.

sources.title: Laki yksityisyyden suojasta työelämässä (759/2004)
sources.establishes: One act for the whole subject, holding processing to what is directly necessary, naming the conditions for cameras and for opening the employer's electronic mail, and putting technical monitoring through a cooperation procedure before it is introduced.

cells.requirement: What each worker is told at installation is the monitoring policy, the purposes, whether personal data are kept and where and for how long, whether the monitoring is permanent, and what the employer and the supervising staff may do.

sources.title: Convention collective de travail n° 81 du 26 avril 2002
sources.establishes: Four purposes for which network communication data may be monitored, collection in the aggregate rather than by name, and individualization as a separate operation with conditions of its own.

cells.requirement: Before the measure starts, those affected are told its purpose, what it will mean in practice, how it will be carried out, and how long it is expected to last.

sources.title: Arbeidsmiljøloven, sections 9-1 and 9-2
sources.establishes: That a control measure needs objective grounds in the undertaking and must not be a disproportionate burden, and that it is discussed with the elected representatives, notified with its expected duration, and evaluated with them at intervals.

cells.requirement: A backup of the mailboxes described in none of the notices given to the staff leaves them unable to know it exists, which is the finding rather than the keeping itself.

sources.title: Provvedimento del 12 marzo 2026, ITAS Mutua
sources.establishes: That an answer given in stages and then handed over in part, without saying what was withheld, does not discharge the right of access, and that a five year backup of employee mail has to be disclosed to the people whose mail it holds.

measures.name: Role-specific training
measures.what: The additional instruction given to managers, privileged users, and the people who run the program.

measures.name: Training records
measures.what: The record, attached to a named person, of the instruction they received and when.

measures.name: Simulated exercises on live staff
measures.what: The testing of the workforce by means of a staged event.

measures.name: Security culture measurement
measures.what: The assessment of what the workforce actually believes and does, as distinct from what it has been told.
